lead: Our biggest update yet. We studied 10 of the most popular faith, food and fitness apps and built what their users asked for most.
s: New in Faith: Search. Type a feeling or a word, like lust, worry, strength or forgiveness, and get verses for it. 26 topics with 10 to 20 verses each, plus a search of every word in the Bible.
Personal records: when you lift more, do more reps or go further than ever before, Manna celebrates it and marks it in History.
Scan a barcode on Eat to log packaged food. Free, no paywall. You can also type the number in.
Download your data from Settings › Data, as a full backup or your workout history as a spreadsheet.
Works offline: once loaded, Manna and the Bible open without internet. Fonts now load from Manna itself, so text looks right straight away.
The phone status bar now matches your theme, and a soft fade sits behind the pinned buttons at the top.
Quick now uses swipe to delete, like Meals and History, instead of a red Remove button on every food.
Loading screens (the welcome, Making with AI, and Friends) now sit in the middle of your screen.
Fixed: calories in Meals line up on the right again.
Meet Manna PRO: $7 a month or $70 a year. See exactly what you get in Settings, under Manna PRO, where Free and PRO are compared side by side.

PRO unlocks unlimited AI, making workouts, schedules and goal plans with AI, fixing foods with AI, unlimited food photos, every theme and music mood, comparing workouts, your full history, unlimited saved routines and bloodwork tracking.
History has a new stats card you can swipe through: Today, This week, This month and This year. Each shows a graph, how many workouts you logged, your total time and your top 2 workout types.
When you make something with AI, the pop-up no longer shows a difficulty and length line.
Treadmill is now a kind of workout and in the gym equipment list, with two new treadmill workouts: an incline walk and run intervals.

Every page switch has a smooth animation that slides in from the side you are heading to. It adapts to your phone: a full slide on fast phones, a lighter one on older phones, and none if Reduce Motion is on.
The Bible now shows the words of Jesus in red, like a red-letter Bible, across the Gospels, Acts and Revelation.

The welcome animation now matches your theme: your theme's own picture draws itself across the whole screen, like the plant growing for Garden or the dumbbell for Fitness. The Fitness theme also has its own picture on Home now.
Sections have shorter names: Eat, Meals, Foods, Quick, Safety and Nutrients in Fuel; Schedule, History and Create in Fitness; Daily in Faith.
Buttons now use small, subtle capitals.
If you finish a workout that lasted under 20 seconds, Manna asks whether to save it to your history, in case it was a mis-tap.
Friends can now see the water you log today, alongside your food and workouts (when you share food). Workout times now show correctly for friends too.

Better on iPhone, especially from the Home Screen: the workout screen now fits your screen exactly, so you no longer scroll the page up and down to line it up, and pages no longer bounce or resize as Safari's bars move.
Swipe to delete is smoother, and swiping a row all the way now deletes it straight away, even when the Delete button is already showing.
Free still has everything you need every day: logging food and workouts, the verse of the day and Bible, Friends and sharing, and the workout and rest timers.

t: Swipe to delete, share with friends
s: Swipe left on a workout in History or a food in Today's meals to delete it, just like in Apple's apps. Swipe a little to show Delete, or all the way to delete straight away.
History has an Edit button. Tap it, select sessions, then delete them all at once or share them.
Share workouts with friends: tap Share on any workout or history session and pick friends. What friends send you shows on the Friends page under Shared with you, where you can save it to My workouts.
New music: Friends has its own warm, upbeat track, and Faith now has a soft choir and organ sound.
The search box for workouts is bigger and easier to use.
Swiping between pages is smoother: the page no longer resizes on every frame while you swipe.
The time and date at the top now match the settings and music buttons: the same rounded shape, colour and size.

t: Right verse of the day, simpler AI schedules
s: Fixed: the verse of the day now always matches YouVersion for your own date. In the evening Manna used to show the wrong verse, because the server was already on the next day.
When you finish an exercise, Manna now takes you to the first exercise that still has sets left, starting from the top, instead of just the next one down.
A small hint at the top of your workout shows that you can swipe right to see your time, sets and controls. It goes away once you have looked.

After AI logs a food from a photo or text, you can fix it right there: change the size with − and +, type the real calories, or tell AI what was different (like “big bowl, no cheese”) and it re-estimates.
Fixed: a sharp noise when leaving the app. Sounds now fade out smoothly when you switch away and fade back in when you return.
Make your own now has a red Delete button for an imported routine you do not want. Tap it twice to remove it.
Browse foods no longer shows the “Showing 60 of 7505” count.
The rainbow outline around the screen while AI works is gone. The Making with AI pop-up is still there.

Make a schedule with AI no longer shows a difficulty and length under the button. Just type what you want, like “4 days a week, 45 minutes, beginner”, and AI follows it. If you do not say, it picks intermediate and 30 to 45 minute sessions.
Fixed: logging a set no longer jumps you back to the first exercise on iPhone. You stay on the exercise you are doing.
The workout screen now only updates the parts that change when you log, so it feels quicker and does not flash.

t: Faster Friends, smoother swipes and fixes
s: Difficulty labels (easy, intermediate, advanced) are now lowercase.
Build with AI no longer has a Length picker. If you want a set length, type it in the box, like “30 minutes”. Otherwise AI picks a sensible length.
Fixed: tapping a difficulty under Make it again as no longer changes the difficulty for every workout you build after.
Imported and self-made routines now have a red delete button on their card. Tap it, then tap Delete? to confirm.
The music button at the top now matches the settings button.
Friends opens instantly: Manna remembers your friends list on your phone and loads the latest in the background. The first time, a loading screen shows while it loads.
Swiping between pages is smoother, especially swiping right to left. Manna now keeps only the pages right next to you ready, instead of waking every page at the start of a swipe.

t: AI glow, bodyweight button and more
s: Anything made with AI now has its own animation: a colourful glow flows around the edge of the screen while AI is working, then flashes when it is done.
New setting: Keep the workout clock running when I leave. Turn it on in Settings and your workout time keeps counting even if you leave Manna or lock your phone. It is off by default.
When you set up a workout, tap All bodyweight to tick Bodyweight for every exercise at once. Tap it again to untick them all.
In the 3 2 1 countdown, the yellow and red circles now drain around the ring just like the green one.
The welcome text on the opening animation is back in capitals, like before.
Text across Manna is easier to read. Capitals are now only used for small, important labels, like section names, the date, Bible references and warnings. Everything else is normal text.
Long lines wrap more evenly, so you get fewer single words left on their own line.
Workout numbers, labels and how-to headings now use normal text instead of capitals.

On iPhone and iPad, a step-by-step guide shows how to add Manna to your Home Screen so it opens full screen like an app. It knows if you are in Safari, Chrome or another app's browser and shows the right steps, with pictures of what to tap.
Manna now runs as a proper full-screen app from the Home Screen, with its own icon and the status bar handled properly.
Find the guide any time in Settings › About.
The workout countdown is now 3 in green, 2 in yellow and 1 in red, with no Go, text or Skip button.

When you import a workout or schedule and Manna cannot read some lines, AI now reads them for you straight away, with no button to tap (it uses one AI use). If you have no AI uses left, the lines are listed like before.
Swiping between pages and scrolling through workouts is smoother. Manna does less work while your finger moves, and drops the blur effect during swipes, so it no longer stutters on older phones.
Workouts are back on the black Apple Fitness background, whatever theme you use. The bottom bar stays hidden during a workout.
Delete account now matches your theme instead of being red.
The Settings gear is smaller, the same size as the music button, and the music button now sits right next to it at the top left.

t: Goals, AI schedules, smarter food scores, sounds
s: Every button at the bottom now makes the same pop as Home. Choose Pop, Bubble, Click, Chime or Wood in Settings › Look › Tap sound.
New background music on Fuel: a light, warm groove with marimba and soft brushes.

Smarter food scores: whole foods score higher and highly processed ones lower, foods with your allergies score 1, very big portions lose points, and scores follow your goals (filling foods for losing weight, calorie-dense protein for gaining, good carbs for endurance).
New Goals card in Settings › Body: set a target weight and a pace (Gentle, Steady or Faster) and see roughly when you could reach it.
Whenever your goals change, a pop-up shows exactly what changes: calories, protein, carbs and fat, workouts a week, focus, reps and workout length. Keep the changes or undo them.
Set goals with AI: describe what you want in your own words, or let AI refine your current goals using your body, progress and workouts.
Make a schedule with AI (PRO): describe your ideal week and AI builds a full 7-day schedule. Rename the schedule and each workout before you save it.
Setup now asks for your pace and an optional target weight, and lets AI pick your goals from a description.
Easy, Intermediate and Hard are colour coded green, orange and red.
Workouts now sit on your theme's background, the bottom bar is hidden during a workout, and there are no scroll sounds while you train.
New Fitness theme: the black and green Apple Fitness look for the whole app. Pick it in Settings › Look › Change theme.
Logging a set keeps you on the same exercise. Manna moves on only when all its sets are done.
Adding or removing a set is now just − and +.
Removed Last time from workout cards.
The How to do it steps now fade away gently when you close them.
When AI finds your food, from text or a photo, the food itself shows first. Swipe to see today's totals.
Buttons that remove or delete are red, and buttons that add are green.
Settings moved out of the bottom bar to a gear at the top left of the screen, coloured to match your theme.

Compare your workouts in History: for any workout you have done more than once, see your last 5 times side by side, including time, sets, volume and your best set for each exercise, with improvements in green.

t: Apple Fitness-style workouts, Friends button, sounds and more
s: How to do it is now a small i button next to each exercise name. Tap it to show or hide the steps.
Removed the Workouts card from Home. Today's plan already shows today's workout with a Start button.
Removed Check in from Today's plan, so it is now eat, train, and read.
Friends now has its own button in the bottom bar, between Fuel and Faith.
New sound effects: a swish when you swipe between pages, a tick for each card in swipe feeds, and soft ticks as you scroll. Turn them off in Settings › Look › Sound effects.
Fixed the time and date at the top running together.
Done sounds: a chime when something is saved or logged, a tiny ding for each set, and a little fanfare when you finish a workout.
Notifications now drop in from the top middle of the screen, like on an iPhone, then fade away.
Less small print: page subtitles and toggle descriptions are hidden, except for eating safeguards and what friends can see.

Workouts now look and feel like Apple Fitness: a 3, 2, 1 countdown before you start, a dark screen, a big yellow timer showing your time and the planned length, and a colourful card for each exercise with a sets ring, + and − buttons for weight and reps, and a big Log set button.
Swipe right during a workout for controls: time, calories, sets, Pause or Resume, Finish, and Resume later, which keeps your workout paused while you use the rest of Manna.
The last card is a Done card with your time, calories and sets, and a big green Done button.

12 new hard template workouts: Heavy Strength Day, Leg Day Destroyer, Upper Body Burner, Bodyweight Gauntlet, Calisthenics Strength, HIIT Inferno, Kettlebell Crusher, Speed Intervals, Hill Sprint Session, Dumbbell Full-Body Blast, Core Crusher and Court Conditioning.
Build with AI now lets you pick Easy, Intermediate or Hard and a length from 15 to 90 minutes before it makes the workout. After it is made, you can remake it at another difficulty.
Manna now plays soft background music, made live in the app (no downloads): calm on most pages, peaceful with chimes on Faith, and an upbeat beat on Fitness. It blends smoothly when you switch.
Tap ♪ next to the clock at the top to turn it on or off, and set the volume in Settings › Look.
It starts after your first tap, pauses when you leave Manna, and goes quiet while the Bible is being read aloud.
Tapping Home, Fitness, Fuel, Faith or Settings at the bottom now makes a little pop, a different note for each. Turn it off in Settings › Look › Tap sounds.
During a workout, each exercise is now its own full-screen card. Swipe up for the next exercise and down to go back, or tap the dots on the side.
The top bar keeps your time, sets logged, Pause and Finish in view the whole time.
After you log the last set of an exercise, Manna moves you to the next card on its own.
The rest timer now pops up on top of whatever card you are on, with a countdown ring, +15 s and Skip rest. Your phone buzzes when rest is over (where supported).

t: AI progress bar, free exercise steps
s: Whenever Manna asks AI for something, the pop-up shows a progress bar and a percentage, and fills to 100% when it is done.
Every exercise without built-in steps, including in AI-made, imported and your own workouts, now gets How to do it steps automatically. These never use your AI uses.
Every exercise now has a How to do it button that opens short, plain steps: how to set up, the movement, and a form tip.
It shows on workout pages, on Before you start and during the workout itself.
Workouts made with AI come with their own steps for each exercise, at no extra AI use.
Exercises you added yourself or imported get exact steps automatically, for free.
If you close Manna, switch apps or lock your phone during a workout, the timer pauses on its own, and so does any rest timer.
When you come back, a pop-up shows your time so far with a Resume button. You can also finish the workout or leave it paused.
Even if your phone closes Manna completely, your workout and the sets you logged come back, with the timer stopped at the moment you left.

t: Faith, one verse at a time
s: Faith is now a full-screen feed. Swipe up for the next verse, starting with the verse of the day, your favorite verse and one chosen for your day.
Double-tap a verse, or tap the heart, to save it. Your saved verses have their own Saved tab, and the Bible reader and prayer notes are under Bible.
Share sends a verse with its reference, and Chapter opens it in the Bible reader.

New accounts no longer start with sample data: no peanut allergy, lab results, knee injury, sleep numbers or coach message. If you set up Manna before today and do not have a peanut allergy, turn it off in Settings › Allergies.
In setup, no goal is picked for you and you can unpick any goal, so choosing only Gain lean muscle is one tap. Your name is marked optional.

t: Making with AI, right where you are
s: Build with AI no longer jumps you to another section. A Making with AI animation pops up right where you tapped, then shows what it made.
For workouts you can Start now, Save to library, or Make another straight from the pop-up, including when no template matches your filters or your search.
Logging food with AI (typed or photo) and reading a workout or schedule with AI show the same animation while they work.
On iPhone and other phones, pinching or double-tapping no longer zooms the page, and tapping into a text box no longer zooms in, so everything stays in view.
To make text bigger, use Settings › Look › Display size on phones, or Aa in the Bible reader.
New Friends page (Today › Friends). Pick a username, then add friends by their username. There is no public search, so only people you tell can find you.
Friends must accept your request before they see anything.
See your friends' workouts this week and their streak, plus what they ate today and their weight change if they choose to share those.
You choose what friends can see: workouts are on by default, food and weight change are off until you turn them on. Friends never see your actual weight.
Send a friend 🙏, 💪 or 🔥 once a day each. You can remove or block anyone.
Friends needs an account. Everything else in Manna still works without one.
The Bible reader works more like YouVersion: tap the book and chapter at the top to pick from a grid of books and chapters, and use the arrows to move between chapters.
Tap any verse to highlight it in 5 colours, copy it, share it or add a note. Highlights sync to your other devices.
Listen: Manna reads the chapter aloud and follows along verse by verse.
Aa: change the text size and pick a serif or sans font.
A reading streak shows how many days in a row you have read.
Removed the extra Change theme button from Settings › You. The big theme tile in Settings › Look is still there.
The footer now reads © 2026 morningfall.
A new Today's plan card at the top of Today puts the whole day in one place: eat (protein first), train, read and reflect, and a quick check-in.
Repeat yesterday's breakfast, lunch, dinner or snacks with one tap, from Today's plan or Quick add.
Short on time? Today's plan suggests a 15-minute workout that fits your equipment.
Write private prayer notes. They are listed on the Faith page, and only you can see them.
Check in with Hard, Okay or Good and get one simple suggestion for tomorrow.
Missed a few days? Manna welcomes you back with no guilt and no catching up.

t: Share foods, cups and spoons, easier search
s: Share a food, a saved meal, a recipe or today's meals with anyone. On phones it opens your share sheet (Messages, AirDrop and more); elsewhere it copies a link.
Opening a shared link shows the foods with their nutrition and allergy warnings, and lets you log them or save them to Quick add.
Shared links carry only food names and nutrition, nothing else from your account.
Your weight is now saved with the date each time you change it, with a trend line in Settings › Goals. It syncs between devices.
Food amounts can now be entered in cups, tablespoons and teaspoons as well as grams and ounces.
Food search is more forgiving: plurals, small typos and other names (fries and chips, soda and cola, yoghurt and yogurt) still find the food.
Setup now says clearly that no account is needed.

Added a Wrestling category with 10 template workouts: takedown drills, conditioning, bottom escapes, neck and grip, strength, explosive power, match simulation, aerobic base, mobility and a no-equipment circuit.
Each shows its muscle groups on the body diagram, and you can pick Wrestling in setup and search.
Pop-ups like What’s new, sign-in, updates and your logged foods now spring open, with their content cascading in and a soft shine, and slide away when closed.
New Graphics and animations setting in Settings › Look: Auto, Low, Medium or High, just for this device. Auto picks for you and switches to a lighter level if a device struggles.
Blurring behind a pop-up now waits until it has opened, which keeps the opening smooth.
Fast logging: Speak it uses your microphone to log a meal by voice.
Photo snaps your plate and AI adds each food.
Import workout file adds a finished run, ride, walk or swim from a .gpx or .tcx file (from Strava, Garmin, Apple Watch apps and more). It counts toward your history and streak.
Removed the Community page and its demo challenges and friends.
Fixed the streak flame not showing on the Workouts page.
The small page tabs at the top (like Workouts, Schedule, History) are easier to read in dark themes.
The old, empty More page now opens Settings, and no longer leaves a box around the Settings tab.
Updated the Weekly schedule intro to match how schedules work now.
Imported and AI-built workouts now show their muscle groups on the body diagram, even when exercises are written differently, like Incline DB press or Tricep pushdowns.
The AI and import previews show the diagram too, before you save.
Removed the Change my picks button from Workouts. Templates has its own page.

Importing a routine or schedule from text understands many more ways of writing: 4x8 squats, 3 sets of 10 bench @ 135lb, 20 push ups, plank 1:30, 5k run, curls 3x8-12, 3 rounds of a list, numbered and bulleted lists, and more.
If some lines still cannot be read, tap Read it with AI (one AI use).
Tap the name of an imported routine, schedule or new workout in the preview to rename it before saving.
On phones, every page with several sections now works TikTok style: Settings pages, Saved workouts, What are you eating, Weekly schedule and more. Swipe up or down to move one section at a time.
Dots on the right show where you are. Long sections scroll normally first.
Weekly schedule now starts empty. Tap Add a schedule to make one.
Free accounts get 1 schedule and PRO accounts up to 3. Schedules you already made are kept.
You can delete a schedule, and adding a workout to a schedule makes one if you have none.

t: Swipe up and down between sections
s: On Workouts › Make your own, the three sections (Make your own, Build with AI, Import from text) are now full-height, TikTok style. Swipe up or down to move one section at a time.
Dots on the right show where you are, and a Next hint at the bottom shows what is below. Long sections scroll normally first.
Settings › About has a new Updates card: see your version and the latest one, check for updates, and update with one tap.
When a newer version is out, a reminder stays at the top of Home until you update.
Weekly schedule has a new Import a schedule from text card. Paste a plan like Monday: Push Day, Tue/Thu - run or Sunday: rest.
Each day is matched to your workouts, and exercises listed under a day become a new workout.
You see a preview and can change any day before it is added to the selected schedule.

t: Build with AI is AI only
s: Build with AI no longer shows a ready-made template first. You only see the workout the AI builds.
If AI is unavailable or you are out of AI uses, it says so instead of showing a template.
Notifications now slide in at the top left, stay a moment, and slide back out, like Minecraft’s. Each has an icon and a heading: Done, Heads up, Removed.
Tap one to dismiss it early. Up to three stack at once.
Automatic sync no longer shows a notification.
Change theme in Settings › Look is now a big, colourful button showing your current theme and every theme’s colour.
The Change theme button on your profile stands out too.

t: Display size for phones and computers
s: Settings › Look now has two display size sliders: one for phones and one for laptops and computers.
Each device uses the one that fits its screen, and both sync to your other devices.
Sizes now go down to 80%.
Finishing setup now always starts the tutorial, including when you run setup again from Settings.
The last setup screen says the tour is next, and the button reads Finish and take the tour.
Saving to your account was being refused by the database (error 403), so nothing was syncing, including themes. That is fixed: your data now saves and syncs between devices.
Signing in on a device that already has its own data no longer asks which copy to keep. Both are combined: workouts and meals from both are kept, and for each setting the most recent change wins.
Devices that were waiting on that question now sync straight away.
If sync ever fails, Settings › Account says why.
The version log now goes all the way back to Version 1.
Versions 1 to 52 are rebuilt from memory and marked approximate. Versions 1 to 59 came before the current site, so they are dated Before Nov 6, 2026.
Your theme and other settings now sync reliably: the most recent change from any device wins.
Sync now in Settings works and tells you when it is done. The Sync line shows when it last synced.
The rest timer only runs between sets of the same exercise. Workouts without sets, like a run, have no rest timer.
During a workout, tap + Add set to add a set to any exercise. Logging an extra set counts it too.
A small test release to try the relaunch-to-update message. Nothing else changed.

t: Plan your sets before you start
s: Before you start now lets you set the sets, reps (or time) and weight for every exercise.
During the workout, change reps and weight on any set, and add or remove sets with + and −.

t: Log a whole meal with AI
s: Describe a meal or snap your plate and AI adds every food at once, for one AI use.
A pop-up shows your calories eaten against today’s goal, with protein, carbs and fat rings, then each food to swipe through. Change the amount or remove a food right there.
Every food gets an emoji.
Today’s meals shows the same rings and a simple list. Tap a food to see what is in it.
The Today’s meals button on What are you eating is gone, since it has its own page.
A Duolingo-style streak counter is now on Home and on Workouts: a flame, your days in a row, and this week’s workout days.
The flame grows when you finish a workout and it pops when your streak goes up.
Turn it off any time under Settings › Data › Extras.
When a newer version of Manna is out, a message asks you to relaunch so you get it.
PRO accounts have no daily AI limit.
The verse in empty space now sits just above the footer.
When you are logged in, everything syncs on its own: your theme and settings, workouts done, food logged, your own and saved workouts, schedules, checklist and AI estimates.
Changes are saved to your account within a few seconds, and changes from your other devices show up within about 30 seconds, without reloading.
If two devices change things at the same time, both sets of changes are kept.
Feedback now goes to themorningfallcorp@gmail.com.
The minimum age is now 10, with no maximum shown.
The Manna footer with the version number now sits at the bottom of every page, not just Home.
Describe a whole meal, like "two eggs, toast and orange juice", or snap a photo of your plate, and AI adds each food to today.
Each food uses one AI use. If you run out partway, Manna adds what it can and tells you what is left.
A single food still opens so you can check the amount before adding it.

t: A verse in the quiet spaces
s: When a page is shorter than your screen, the empty space now shows a short verse that matches your theme.
It uses the same colours as the Saved workouts note, and changes with your theme and each day.
The page bar on Workouts and Settings no longer says how many pages are left. The dots show where you are.
Each swipe now moves exactly one page, like flicking a card, instead of scrolling through several.
A small nudge springs back to the page you were on.
Workouts is now four pages you swipe between: Saved, Make your own, Templates and Search.
Ready-made workouts are now called template workouts.
Settings is split into five pages: You, Look, Body, Data and About.
The bar on top shows the page you are on and its icon. Tap a dot to jump to a page.
Pages tilt a little as you swipe, like flicking a card. Reduce motion turns this off.
Tapping a search result opens the workout again.
Settings › Account shows how you signed in: Google, Apple or email, with your name from Google.
Sign in with Google is now switched on.
Setup’s first screen lets you sign in to bring your data back, or create an account.
Switch to a different account from Settings › Account.
The Signed out message is now red so it is easy to spot.
The first time you open Manna after this update, you are invited to create a free account.
Sign in with email today. Apple and Google sign-in appear as soon as they are switched on.
You can skip it and sign in later from Settings › Account.
Create an account in Settings to keep your data safe and use Manna on all your devices.
Your data syncs automatically while you are logged in.
AI uses are counted on your account, so they follow you between devices.
Settings now explains clearly where your data is kept.
AI features now use Google’s current Gemini model, so Build with AI and food estimates work.
AI answers faster, and a slow answer stops after 25 seconds instead of hanging.
Build with AI and food estimates now use a real AI model, including food photos.
You get 5 AI uses a day. After that, workouts are built from Manna’s own rules.
Settings has a Version log of every update. The All pages list is gone.
Removed the Or describe it in words button from Fitness.
After each update, this screen shows what changed.
Scroll down for every past update, or open it any time from Settings.
The Bible and credits section in Settings is now just Credits.
Your targets on Fuel no longer show the protein-per-kg line.
Switching kg and lb in setup no longer replays the animation.
The top 3 workouts counter fills in three dots as you pick and stays in view.

t: History at a glance and rest choice
s: History shows date, time, workout and length, in the workout’s colour. Tap one for every detail.
Each set records how long it took.
Before you start asks how long to rest between sets, or no rest, and remembers it.
Build a workout from scratch, edit a copy of any ready-made one, or paste it as text.
Set sets, reps or time, and weight for every exercise.
Pick several muscles at once. If nothing fits, build one by hand or with AI.
Saved workouts come first when planning your schedule, and you choose which schedule to add to.
Turn schedules on or off in Settings, and see each workout’s difficulty at a glance.
Removed the line of text under the Manna logo.
Tapping a workout type moves straight to the next question.
When a workout is due today, it opens Fitness with its muscles and a Start button.
Workout history starts empty and only shows workouts you finish.
Send feedback from Settings.
Fitness shows your last 3 workouts.
Save any workout to find it again quickly.
The setup top 3 picker uses the same cards as Fitness.
The app is now simply called Manna.
The tabs are Home, Fitness, Fuel, Faith and Settings.
Manna opens much faster and animations are smoother, especially on older phones.
Frosted Surfaces off now has a proper solid look and no longer breaks the welcome screens.
Picking your top 3 workouts uses tiles instead of a text list.
Fresh icon files so Safari shows the Manna loaf.
Safari-friendly tab icons.
Safari keeps the real tab icon.
Manna opens straight into your theme.
The home page footer shows the current version.
Add Manna to your iPhone home screen with its own icon.
A solid black and white loaf with a cross.
The scored-loaf logo arrives in the header and splash screen.
Choosing a sport shows every workout for it.
New verse of the day.
Setup and the splash screen always use the Default theme.
A welcome screen, a guided tutorial, and workout filters in setup.
Setup no longer assumes your name.
The verse of the day updates live.

t: Sports, search and Build with AI
s: Ten sports with 3+ workouts each, search on Workouts home, Build with AI on home, easy-to-hard sort, Configure with level and focus.
Released together with Version 60.
